processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) ingots produced from raw materials with high purity (>99.9 %) using a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere.
Homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h prior to hot rolling.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Plates cut into 10×5×2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching — defines the solid-solution (soft) state of the 17Al alloy.

structures.overall_structure: Single α (BCC) phase; no γ (FCC) region resolved in the solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Coarse grain structure; IPF map of the solution-treated 17Al alloy dominated by one large (green) grain surrounded by differently oriented neighbours (200 µm scale bar)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness, load 9.8 N for 15 s, average of 5 measurements
Elastic modulus measured through compressive stress-strain curves; used as input E in the indentation fracture-toughness Eq. (1)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the solution-treated (and subsequently aged) 17Al alloy samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated 17Al alloy hardness = 259.8 ± 1.5 HV (Table 3); hardness of solution-treated alloys increased with rising Al content.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the constituent phases and their distribution of the solution-treated (and aged) alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels (including 17Al) consist of a single α (BCC) phase (uniformly red phase maps, Fig. 3).

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure chemical composition of the alloys (Table 1)
characterization_methods.key_findings: EDS composition of the 17Al alloy (at.%): Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0.

unmapped_findings: EDS-measured chemical composition of the 17Al alloy (at.%, Table 1): Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0; nominal Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) (b0013, b0017).

The 17Al alloy in the solution-treated (solid-solution) state is a single α (BCC) phase with a coarse grain structure (Fig. 3b), and its solution-treated hardness of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV is higher than that of the 15Al alloy because the hardness of the solution-treated alloys increased with rising Al content, attributed to solid-solution strengthening (b0036).

For high-Al Fe-Mn-Al-based alloys, precipitation of the D0₃ phase after solution treatment and quenching is common, and the increase in Al content increases the amount/size of D0₃; however, the D0₃ phase was not observed in the alloys with maximum hardness, suggesting its depletion accompanied β-Mn precipitation and growth (b0065).
